scenes.headline: Three zero-days. One VPN. Root access.
scenes.say: Companies on Ivanti VPNs: attackers chained three zero-days. Here is how the attack worked, and why one patch was not enough.

scenes.headline: The box that lets staff work from home
scenes.body: Ivanti Connect Secure: an SSL VPN appliance at the edge of company networks
scenes.say: Ivanti Connect Secure is an SSL VPN. It is the box that lets employees reach the company network from home, so it sits right on the internet.

scenes.headline: Three weeks, three flaws

items.text: Attacks begin on a fully patched appliance
Ivanti discloses and fixes the first flaw
CISA adds them to its exploited list

scenes.say: Researchers at Volexity say the attacks began on October third, against an appliance that was fully patched. On October thirteenth, Ivanti disclosed and fixed the first flaw. On October twenty-ninth, it patched two more. And on October thirtieth, the US cyber agency CISA added them to its list of known exploited bugs.

scenes.headline: From no login to full control
items: Run code through an upload race · same CVE
scenes.say: The chain had three steps. First, bypass the login check. Then, run code through a file upload race. Finally, escalate to root, full control of the device, without ever logging in.

scenes.headline: Passwords, and the keys to locked laptops
scenes.body: Stored LDAP credentials taken · Active Directory searched for LAPS admin passwords and BitLocker recovery keys
scenes.say: Once inside, the attackers took stored credentials, then searched Active Directory for local admin passwords and BitLocker recovery keys, the keys that unlock encrypted laptops.

scenes.headline: Ivanti's Integrity Checker missed it
scenes.body: No web shell · logs edited · code changed only in memory
scenes.say: And it was hard to spot. No web shell was left behind, logs were edited, and code was changed only in memory. Ivanti's own Integrity Checker Tool missed it.

scenes.headline: Patched in October? Patch again.
scenes.body: Versions fixed on Oct 13, such as 22.8R2.5, are still open to the two newer flaws. Fixed: 25.1.1.3 · 22.8R2.6
scenes.say: Here is the catch. If you patched on October thirteenth, you are not done. Those versions are still open to the two newer flaws. The fixed versions are on screen.

scenes.headline: to patch the root flaw and check for compromise
scenes.source: CISA via Help Net Security · Security Affairs
scenes.say: CISA gave US federal agencies until November second to fix the root flaw and check for compromise, and until November thirteenth for the third one.

scenes.headline: Your VPN is the front door.
scenes.body: Patch it like an emergency, and watch it with your own monitoring. A clean scan is not proof.
scenes.say: Analyst note: your VPN is the front door, and attackers keep testing it. Patch it like an emergency, and watch it with your own network monitoring, because a clean scan is not proof.

scenes.headline: What to do this week
items: Upgrade every appliance to a fixed release
Don't trust a clean Integrity Checker scan alone
Preserve memory and logs before rebooting
If compromise is suspected, rotate credentials
scenes.say: What to do this week. Upgrade every Connect Secure appliance to a fixed release. Don't trust a clean Integrity Checker scan on its own. Preserve memory and logs before you reboot or reset. And if you suspect compromise, rotate the exposed credentials.
